summary: Independently accepted on 2026-09-23: retain three outward reuse links to PDE and OptimalTransport and four scope/comparison proposals. The original catalogue-wide screen covers 217 other records; the review searched all nine focal stages against the current 2007-stage world and found no additional direct contract. Seven pinned declaration statements were independently checked. Abstract real-Banach C0 generation is existing library work; concrete heat realizations, carrier comparisons and arbitrary ACP-solution uniqueness are separate obligations. Acceptance concerns this dependency map, not proof closure or approval of stale mathematical claims in the focal README.

verifiedLibrary.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup
verifiedLibrary.statement: Real Banach space; bounded real-linear operators indexed by nonnegative time; semigroup identities and pointwise continuity at zero.

verifiedLibrary.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.hilleYosida_generation_iff
verifiedLibrary.statement: General real-Banach characterization with 1<=M, dense domain, real resolvent half-line and all n>=1 power bounds. HasGrowthBound takes omega then M.

verifiedLibrary.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.eq_of_generator_eq
verifiedLibrary.statement: Two actual C0 semigroups on the same real Banach space are equal when their LinearPMap generators are equal.

verifiedLibrary.name: TauCeti.hausdorff_bernstein_widder_existsUnique
verifiedLibrary.statement: IsContinuousCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi is equivalent to unique finite Laplace representation; not smoothness at zero.

verifiedLibrary.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.norm_apply_le_map_zero_re_of_star_eq_neg
verifiedLibrary.statement: Norm bound at a requires the explicit hypothesis star a=-a on an additive group.

verifiedLibrary.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.isClassicalSolution_realOperator
verifiedLibrary.statement: The orbit of a generator-domain vector is a classical solution: continuous derivative within the nonnegative half-line, right-sided at zero and two-sided at positive times. This is an existence statement, not uniqueness of arbitrary solution curves.

verifiedLibrary.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.isMildSolution_realOperator
verifiedLibrary.statement: Every orbit is continuous and satisfies the integrated Cauchy equation with integral in the generator domain.

links.reason: Reuse the existing real-Banach C0-semigroup carrier, its generator with dense LinearPMap domain, and the unbounded-resolvent interface for the concrete heat semigroup. PDE owns the chosen Lp realization, domain and closed-generator identification, heat kernel, boundary conditions and smoothing estimates. The scalar heat kernel alone does not establish strong continuity in a chosen Banach norm. This is a carrier/API dependency, distinct from the separately indexed Hille-Yosida theorem. The supplier is already present at the pinned Tau Ceti commit; it is not a request to rebuild it. The pinned StronglyContinuousSemigroup structure itself does not bundle a growth bound; use HasGrowthBound separately where needed, despite the parenthetical in the source quotation.

evidence.quote:
**Semigroups.** The **heat semigroup**, generators, and **Hille–Yosida**; the heat
    kernel on `ℝⁿ` (consume the Fourier transform) and the smoothing estimates.

links.reason: The general generation theorem supplies the abstract Hille-Yosida assertion named in F.26. For each concrete operator PDE must prove dense domain, real resolvent half-line and every required power estimate with 1 <= M and omega real; the theorem does not supply those heat-operator estimates. Use TauCeti.Semigroups.hilleYosida_generation_iff at the pin, whose growth predicate takes omega before M. The roadmap claim that the theorem is build-here is stale. Its contraction-only Yosida sentence cannot be used as the proof of the general-growth theorem.

links.reason: OT item 9 explicitly imports the abstract linear C0/contraction carrier and compares closed generators before invoking semigroup uniqueness. Reuse StronglyContinuousSemigroup and eq_of_generator_eq from the pinned library, after constructing two actual linear strongly continuous semigroups on the same real Banach space and identifying their full generator domains and maps. Agreement on a test core needs a closure/core theorem first. Restriction to probability densities and agreement with the nonlinear Wasserstein flow remain OT work. Heat on all finite signed measures with total-variation norm is not automatically C0; L1 densities are a viable stated realization. No arbitrary nonlinear EVI flow is made linear by this link.

overlaps.detail: F.26 lists abstract generators and Hille-Yosida alongside its concrete heat construction; Part A and its dedicated milestone already own that abstract theory, and the reviewed library audit plus pinned source show it implemented.
overlaps.proposal: Keep the general C0, generator, resolvent and generation interface with OneParameterSemigroups and consume its existing Tau Ceti declarations. Rescope PDE F.26 to concrete heat carriers, dense domains/cores, resolvent estimates, boundary conditions, kernels and smoothing. The explicit ownership paragraph near the end of OptimalTransport already requests this split. Do not require completion of every PDE or OT flow before reusing general semigroup theory.

evidence.quote:
generates a C₀ semigroup
of growth `(M, ω)`.

overlaps.detail: The common specialization is a linear Hilbert-space contraction flow, such as the exponential flow of a quadratic energy. OT also builds nonlinear EVI semigroups and Moreau-Yosida minimization maps, which are not LinearPMap resolvents. Its RCD layer needs a separate quadratic-Cheeger-energy comparison.
overlaps.proposal: Keep nonlinear metric-gradient-flow existence, EVI, minimizing movements and flow stability in OT. For a densely defined closed nonnegative quadratic form on a real Hilbert space, make the OT comparison explicitly identify its linear L2 contraction semigroup and generator with the existing C0 carrier; retain the form-domain/density and sign conventions. With generator A=-B for a nonnegative self-adjoint B, the variational resolvent is (I-tau A)^-1 = tau^-1 R(tau^-1,A) for tau>0, not literally R(tau^-1,A). For Phi(x)=||x||^2/2 check x/(1+tau) and exp(-t)x. On RCD spaces construct Cheeger energy, prove quadraticity and the L2-to-probability carrier bridge before the entropy-flow comparison. No hard prerequisite on the whole nonlinear OT10 or RCD14 stage is inferred merely from the word semigroup.

evidence.quote:
for `Φ(x)=‖x‖²/2` on a Hilbert space, the resolvent is
`x ↦ x/(1+τ)` and the flow is `e⁻ᵗx`

Build minimal weak upper gradients, Cheeger energy, its relaxed `W¹,²` domain,
   infinitesimal Hilbertianity, and the associated `L²` heat flow/Dirichlet form.

overlaps.detail: The shared slice is characteristic-function positivity and Fourier normalization, not construction of the named laws. StandardDistributions explicitly computes transforms but excludes redevelopment of general positive-definiteness and Bochner representations.
overlaps.proposal: Keep named probability measures, parameter boundary cases and explicit transform formulas in StandardDistributions. Reuse Mathlib characteristic-function uniqueness and the existing Tau Ceti positivity/convention interface where a positivity or Fourier comparison is actually requested. Specify FourierAtom integral at a = charFun at -2*pi*a. Bochner existence is not a prerequisite for a distribution already constructed by density, product or pushforward, and finite-measure transforms do not imply finite moments or an mgf near zero. The matrices in Gaussian/Wishart positivity are not themselves positive-definite functions on an involutive monoid.

evidence.quote:
A stated **Fourier-convention conversion lemma** between Mathlib's `2π` form
  (`e^{−2πi⟨·,·⟩}`) and the characteristic-function form (`e^{i⟨·,·⟩}`)
This roadmap computes characteristic functions for named distributions but does not redevelop their general positive-definiteness or Bochner representations.

overlaps.detail: Reflection positivity of graph connection matrices and the generic positive-definite-kernel predicate both test nonnegative finite quadratic forms. A graph-gluing monoid is not the particular time-space semigroup in the BCR theorem, and graphon representability has a different proof.
overlaps.proposal: DenseGraphLimits owns labelled graph gluing, isomorphism invariance and the Mobius/exchangeable-law proof of graphon representation. For a reusable positivity comparison, first quotient fixed-k labelled graphs by label-preserving isomorphism, prove a commutative gluing monoid with its identity, and use the identity involution. Complexify its real symmetric PSD connection matrices to compare with the existing generic IsPositiveDefinite/PosSemidef API. Do not infer a BCR representation: its domain, continuity and boundedness hypotheses have not been established for this graph monoid. Do not import the false generic norm bound from the focal README; group-negation and general-monoid cases differ.

evidence.quote: The **PD-function ↔ PD-kernel** equivalence (`K(a,b) = F(a + b⋆)`; `F(a − b)` for a group)

**reflection-positive** (`IsReflectionPositive`) when every such finite connection matrix is positive
semidefinite
